## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want tests that pin how scaled enemy counts reach the campaign (static and sequenced) without breaking determinism or the existing campaign invariants, so the density change cannot silently reshape the authored campaign.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Enemy counts rise with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Add tests (in the existing wave test files, or a new `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts`) that:

- Assert level-1 `LEVELS` wave groups are unchanged by the scaling path (deep-equal counts), so onboarding data stays byte-identical.
- Assert a level-10 group grows by the documented multiplier with the documented rounding, floor of 1, 200-per-group cap, and `single`-formation groups remain exactly 1.
- Assert the scaling is applied to **both** the static `LEVELS` campaign and the sequenced campaign (`buildSequencedLevels`, covering `fixed`, `curve` and `dynamic` generation modes), through the shared build seam.
- Assert same-seed builds remain byte-identical (determinism contract) and that a second build of the same campaign is idempotent (no double scaling).
- Assert the scaled campaign still satisfies the existing invariants and wave-balance rules: `campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `campaignRoster.test.ts`, `waveBalance` R1–R3, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`.
- Assert the shared helper is the only scaling implementation consumed by game and gym launch paths (parity seam), not a duplicated copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD for the specified reason (no scaling applied/nonexistent helper).
- Tests cover level-1 identity, level-10 growth, rounding, floor, cap, `single` groups, both campaign paths, same-seed determinism and no double scaling.
- Tests cover scaled-campaign compliance with the existing campaign invariants and wave-balance rules.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/waves/Formations.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- optionally `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts` (new)
- existing invariant suites: `src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `src/core/waveBalance.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add level-scaling module and tunable rules" (needs the helper contract). Blocks the campaign count-application feature.

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want deterministic tests that prove the kill-time power-up supply falls with the campaign level, so the supply curve cannot regress unnoticed.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Power-up supply per enemy falls with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Extend `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (and the rules tests where appropriate) with tests that:

- Force the scene RNG so the number of drops over N kills is exact and deterministic at level 1 (matches the current 0.18 rate) and at level 10 (matches 0.05, i.e. at most 30 % of the level-1 rate).
- Prove the level is resolved from the live campaign (`WaveManager.currentLevel()?.level`), i.e. after advancing a level the next kills use the new chance, and an unknown level falls back to level 1.
- Prove the small-asteroid Extra Life roll scales by the same ratio and is unchanged at level 1 (`rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`).
- Prove drop types/weights, the mineral kill-drop rule and timed weapon/power-up effects are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD (flat 0.18 roll for every level).
- Assertions are exact and seeded — no statistical/threshold flakiness.
- Coverage includes level 1 identity, level 10 endpoint, mid-run level advance, unknown-level fallback and Extra Life proportionality.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add level-scaling module and tunable rules". Blocks the PlayScene drop-roll feature.

# Goal

As the producer, I want one end-to-end verification item that proves the shipped pure modules collectively satisfy the epic's cross-cutting acceptance criteria (AC1, AC4, AC5) once every axis has landed — each variety axis authored as data consumed by the shipped pure ring/resolver/deployment modules with a real persisted effect, gym↔game parity, and all docs updated. Closing the hex-variety epic runs through this item.

## Context

Part of **Post-MVP Hangar War: hex variety** (AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG). Producer answers Q1 = b, Q2 = a, Q3 = a (2026-11-13). This is the epic-level integration/verification slice, mirroring the parent epic's "Hangar slice end-to-end verification" (AH-0MVUXC2T0009Y42G). Runs after all three axes and the docs item, verifying the epic's own ACs rather than adding new behaviour.

## Scope

- Verify AC1 (data-authored variety): each axis — personalities, contracts, ring landmarks — is authored data in the ring definitions/CSV seeds consumed by the shipped pure ring, resolver and deployment modules; no second deployment, resolver or map implementation (gym↔game parity); no divergent combat code outside the shared combat core.
- Verify AC4 (real, persisted effect): each axis has a gameplay effect resolved by the pure modules and persisted under `ai_hell_hangar_war` with field-presence migration (older saves load safely, no second storage key); determinism preserved; fortress = capturable after two passes; cache = pays bonus salvage instead of granting; contract bonus banked through the existing banking rule on capture.
- Verify AC5 (gym coverage and docs): `GymHexWar`, `GymHangar` and the combat gyms (where a shared personality mechanic lands) exercise the same code as the game; tests pin each axis; the full suite is green; all documentation (GDD §8.2, `OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, code comments, README entries) reflects the shipped state.
- Produce the audit/close evidence: each parent AC mapped to the child/child-ACs that satisfy it, plus the merge/dev-push state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each variety axis (personalities, contracts, ring landmarks) is authored data in the ring definitions/CSV seeds and is consumed by the shipped pure ring, resolver and deployment modules — no second deployment, resolver or map implementation (gym↔game parity). Personalities are config-tunes through the shipped profile seams **plus** the small set of data-driven shared combat mechanics; contracts are per-hex optional objectives paying currency; landmarks are fortress/cache set-pieces on ordinary hexes.
- Each axis has a gameplay effect resolved by the pure modules and persisted under `ai_hell_hangar_war` (field-presence migration: older saves load safely, no second storage key); determinism is preserved. A fortress hex becomes capturable after **two** capture passes; a cache hex pays out bonus salvage instead of granting; a contract bonus is banked through the existing banking rule on capture.
- `GymHexWar` and `GymHangar` (and the combat gyms where a shared personality mechanic lands) exercise the same code as the game — the shared mechanics run identically in the game and in every gym, never as a divergent copy. Tests pin each axis and the full suite is green. All related documentation (GDD §8.2, `OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`) is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and README entries.
- An AC-trace table records, for each parent AC, the child item(s) and their ACs that satisfy it; no parent AC is left with an empty trace.
- The epic is ready to advance: all children complete, the suite is green on dev, and the dev→main promotion path (ship skill) is unblocked.

## Key Files

- src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts + src/data/hex-ring-*.csv — authored variety data (all axes)
- src/core/hangarWar/ — hexRing, hexIntel, hexBoss, captureCycle, hangarWarStore, types (shipped pure modules)
- src/scenes/core/… (shared combat core) + src/scenes/gym/ — parity surface exercised end-to-end
- docs/Game Design Document.md (§8.2), docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md, docs/GYM_PARITY.md

## Related work

- discovered-from: AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG (hex variety epic)
- Depends on: AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7 (vocabulary), AH-0MWEW4RVP002LIP4 (acceptance tests), AH-0MWEW50B10089D4W (personality), AH-0MWEW58WD003NFXS (contract), AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH (landmarks), AH-0MWEW5QCR009NX0V (docs/parity)
- Pattern: AH-0MVUXC2T0009Y42G — Hangar slice end-to-end verification (parent epic)
- AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule

## Verification evidence (2026-11-15)

**Automated gate:** `src/core/hangarWar/hexVarietyEpic.verification.test.ts` — 17 epic-level cases driving the authored variety sample ring through the *shipped* pure modules in sortie order: authored data + validation → generated ring → known-ahead intel → deployment/boss/mini-boss profile → capture cycle → save/load round trip → determinism. Each case names the parent AC it verifies.

**Observation (recorded in the AC trace):** the shipped ring table (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`, rings 1–2) currently authors **no** variety — the vocabulary, validation, resolvers, intel, persistence and docs all ship, and the authored example is the ring-3 variety sample (`src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`). So the machinery is shipped and exercised end to end, but no *shipped* ring hands a player a personality/contract/landmark yet. Authoring it is content/balance work (which hex, which bonus, inside ring 2's survivable band), so it is recorded as the discovered sibling `AH-0MWH4F375000X08G` rather than smuggled into this verification slice.

## AC trace (parent AC → children → evidence)

| Parent AC | Satisfied by | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **AC1** — data-authored variety on the shipped seams | AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7 (vocabulary + CSV mirrors + validation), AH-0MWEW50B10089D4W (personalities), AH-0MWEW58WD003NFXS (contracts), AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH (landmarks) | `hexVarietyEpic.verification.test.ts` AC1 cases (validator accepts shipped rings + sample, axes come from the published vocabulary, `6 × n` geometry unchanged, malformed variety rejected); `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` (CSV parity); `hexPersonalityMechanics.ts` single shared mechanic set |
| **AC2** — known-ahead intel before commitment | AH-0MWEW4RVP002LIP4 (intel contracts), AH-0MWEW50B10089D4W, AH-0MWEW58WD003NFXS, AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH | AC2 cases assert personality + mechanic, contract (objective/bonus/status), landmark (fortress progress, cache meaning) and the tile tags are published on **unheld** hexes by `buildHexMapModel`; `hexIntel.variety.test.ts` |
| **AC3** — loud validation | AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7 | `hexRing.test.ts` variety issues + AC1 malformed cases (unknown personality, empty contract, cache on the weapon hex) through `validateRingDefinitions` |
| **AC4** — real, persisted effect | AH-0MWEW58WD003NFXS (contract fulfilment + banked bonus), AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH (fortress two passes, cache payout), AH-0MWEW4RVP002LIP4 (acceptance contracts) | AC4 cases: contract banks once (replay guard) and publishes `fulfilled`; fortress needs two passes with progress published; cache pays `CACHE_SALVAGE_BONUS` instead of granting and pays once; `parseHangarWarPayload` round trip + field-presence migration for legacy saves; identical replay from the same payload/seed |
| **AC5** — gym coverage and docs | AH-0MWEW50B10089D4W (GymMiniBoss parity), AH-0MWEW5QCR009NX0V (GymHexWar capture parity + docs), AH-0MWEW4RVP002LIP4 | `hexVarietyEpic.verification.test.ts` AC5 cases (deployment from the map's ring, `hexMiniBossConfigForLevel` shared mapping, mechanics signalled by the shared core); `GymHexWar.test.ts` variety/capture cases; `GymMiniBoss.test.ts` parity; `src/hexVarietyDocs.test.ts` + `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` docs guards |

No parent AC has an empty trace. The epic's "ready to advance" line is satisfied once this item's dev push lands green (all children terminal, full suite green on dev, ship path unblocked).

## Impact

The hex-variety epic now has one automated gate that proves the three axes work
end to end through the shipped modules, so reviewers and future changes can see
in one run that personalities, contracts and landmarks are authored, published
ahead of time, resolved and persisted — and that nothing split into a second
implementation.

## Problem

When a driven child spawns but dies before writing anything (spawn-failed), its worktree exists but is clean (`has_changes=False`, `worktree_verdict=CHILD_CLEAN`). The next `phase_parent`/`drive` run then calls `_child_main_checkout_violation()` which scans the main checkout and sibling worktrees. If those surfaces are dirty (unrelated to the spawn-failed child), the violation fires incorrectly, blaming the spawn-failed child for dirt it never produced.

## User Story

As a driver running `implement.py drive` on an epic, I want spawn-failed children to be resettable without the placement guard incorrectly blaming them for unrelated dirt in the main checkout or sibling worktrees.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A spawn-failed child (worktree exists, no changes, no commits ahead) is treated as startable-again/reset, not as a placement violation, so the next `drive` re-spawns it without requiring manual `abort`.
- The placement guard distinguishes 'this child wrote elsewhere' from 'this child wrote nothing and other surfaces happen to be dirty' — the latter must not fail the chain.
- Regression test: a spawn-failed child plus a dirty main checkout and a dirty sibling worktree does not produce a `_child_main_checkout_violation`; a child that genuinely wrote only into a sibling worktree still does.
- No weakening of the genuine cross-worktree-write detection (SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I) — existing tests in `test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` must continue to pass.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_main_checkout_violation` call sites in `phase_parent`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — existing sibling stray tests, add spawn-fail regression

## Tests

1. Spawn-failed child + dirty main checkout + dirty sibling worktree → no violation, drive continues (not blocked)
2. Spawn-failed child + clean surfaces → reported for re-implementation (happy path unchanged)
3. Genuine cross-worktree write → violation still detected (existing test must pass — no weakening)
4. Both `skip-in-progress` and `implement` call paths in `phase_parent` covered by tests
data.title: Test: spawn-failed child with dirty main/sibling is not a placement violation

Parent: AH-0MWCB6021008L4YN (Ring-timing text report prints seed 1's retry, between-sortie and re-capture minutes as if they were the multi-seed figures).

## Goal (user story)

As a ring-timing harness operator, I want every metric line of `formatRingTimingReport` to describe the seed set (not seed 1's sample), so the text report and the JSON artefact agree.

## Summary

`formatRingTimingReport` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from `report.runs[0]` (seed 1) while every other line uses the summary means. Add the missing aggregate stats to `RingTimingSummary`, render from the summary, and regenerate the committed artefact so its JSON summary carries the new fields.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `RingTimingSummary` gains `betweenSortieMinutes`, `retryMinutes`, `retakeMinutes` and `expectedRetakes` as `RingTimingStats` (count/mean/min/max), populated in `simulateRingTiming` via `stats(runs.map(...))`.
- `formatRingTimingReport` renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from the summary aggregates (mean, with min-max where the JSON summary carries them) - never from `report.runs[0]`; a single-seed report still renders that seed's figures under its `seed 1` header.
- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` is regenerated (`npm run ring-timing -- --json --out docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, default rings/lines/seeds 1-3): deterministic, so every existing mean/min/max value is unchanged and the summary merely gains the four new fields; the committed-evidence tests still pass.
- The sibling pinning test (AH-0MWGVXB95002W7KI) passes; the full project test suite passes via the test skill at the dev-push gate.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the `RingTimingSummary` interface and its construction in `simulateRingTiming`.
- Update the three lines of `formatRingTimingReport` to read `summary.*.mean` (min-max where carried), mirroring the `total` line's style.
- Regenerate the committed artefact via the CLI; update the fixture type `CommittedBaselineReport` only if its partial shape needs extending (it already tolerates extra keys).
- Verify via `/skill:test` (never ad-hoc test commands): changed-scope gate, then the committed-evidence suite / full gate.

## Constraints

- Reporting/consistency fix only: no behaviour or measured-value changes; the regenerated artefact's existing totals must be byte-identical in value.
- Additive JSON arity: no exported `RingTimingSummary` field is renamed or removed.
- UK English.

## Risky assumptions

- Regeneration is deterministic (asserted by the existing determinism test): same seeds/options reproduce identical values, so committed totals cannot drift. Success threshold: the regenerated artefact's existing mean/min/max are unchanged.
data.title: Implement: render retry/between-sortie/recapture from the seed aggregate

- The quoted figure equals the mean of the committed per-seed `retryMinutes` (e.g. ring 2 grind: retries ≈12.0 min of the ≈48.1 min mean total, ≈25 % share) and matches the rendered report's retries line.

# Hangar War: leave the defending bot with the run's permanent upgrades

## Problem statement

When a hex deployment is won, the bot left behind carries only the **catalogue** hull rating (`baseDefence + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems` of the hull as authored in the hangar catalogue), so everything the ship actually earned during that sortie — permanent weapon levels, permanent power-up levels and owned consumable charges — is discarded at the moment of victory. A player who clears a hex with a heavily upgraded ship leaves a bot no stronger than a bare hull, which makes the capture's "leave a bot" step feel disconnected from the run that earned it.

## Users and user stories

- **Player (primary).** "When I beat a hex's mini-boss, I want the bot I leave behind to keep the permanent upgrades my ship had at that moment, so the run I just flew is what defends the hex."
- **Player, reading the map.** "When I look at a held hex, I want to see what the defending bot is made of — its upgrade contribution and total rating — so I can judge whether the next frontier attack will hold."
- **Designer/tuner (secondary).** "I want the upgrade → rating conversion in one documented table, so retuning defence strength never needs a code change or a save migration."

## Existing state

- `leaveDefender` (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`) builds the `HexDefender` with `defenceRating = deriveDefenderRating(hullId)`, plus optional boss-typed `skills` from the hull and equipped modifiers.
- `deriveDefenderRating` / `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) are the single rating formula, fed only from the hangar catalogue.
- `HexCaptureInput` carries `hexId`, `defenderHullId`, `salvage`, `definitions`, `banked`, `tuning` — **no run-upgrade snapshot**.
- At the mini-boss victory the run does hold the data: `Player.getWeaponLevels()`, `Player.getPowerUpLevels()`, and `PowerUpLevelStore.snapshotConsumablePools()` (read by `_saveCheckpoint` for the arcade path, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`).
- The defender is never flown; every defence is arithmetic over stored numbers (`resolveDefence`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`).
- Design of record explicitly says the rating comes from the hull's hangar upgrades only: GDD *capture cycle* step 3 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (intake assumption A4). This item changes that rule.
- The frontier aggression budget is sized from `resolvePlayerStrength(hangar)` — hangar progression only — and the *between-sortie tick* compares each held hex's stored rating against `baseAttackingForce (2) + origin aggression × 1`, scaled by `100 + 15 × aggression` % ± 10 %.

## Desired change

1. **Snapshot the run at victory.** `resolveHexCapture` accepts the run's permanent-upgrade snapshot and `leaveDefender` persists it on the `HexDefender` as an **additive optional field** (same back-compat pattern as `skills`): permanent weapon levels, permanent power-up levels, and the owned consumable charge state.
2. **Convert it with the hull's own vocabulary.** The snapshot contributes to the rating through one documented mapping table, so the rating stays a single number the resolver compares:

   | Source | Stat bucket | Weight |
   |---|---|---|
   | every permanent weapon level (any weapon) | firepower | 1 point per level |
   | permanent level of a **defensive** power-up kind (Shield, Force Field, Thorn Field, Bomb, Smart Bomb, Phase Shift) | armour | 1 point per level |
   | permanent level of every other power-up kind (Teleport, Speed Boost, Frenzy, Chrono, Magnet, Mineral Scoop, Mystery UFO, Salvage, Strike, Mining Laser) | systems | 1 point per level |
   | each held **defensive** consumable charge (Shield, Force Field, Thorn Field) | armour | 1 point per charge |
   | each held **other** consumable charge (Mystery UFO) | systems | 1 point per charge |

   Then `defenceRating = hullRating + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems`, reusing the shipped `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` weights so there is still exactly one rating formula.
3. **Show the numbers.** The map's held-hex detail panel and the between-sortie defence report list the bot's stored upgrade breakdown next to the existing hull/skills lines, so a hold or fall that depended on upgrades is legible.
4. **One code path for the game and the gyms.** `GymHexWar`'s "leave bot" control surface takes the same snapshot and renders through the shared helpers (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity); no second derivation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `leaveDefender` / `resolveHexCapture` persist the run's permanent-upgrade snapshot on the `HexDefender` and derive `defenceRating = hullRating + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems`, where the stat buckets come from one exported, documented mapping table that classifies **every** `WeaponId` and `PowerUpId` (a test fails if a catalogue id is unclassified).
- A defender captured with no permanent upgrades produces exactly today's payload and today's `defenceRating` (the new field is omitted when empty), so existing saves, fixtures and replays are unchanged; a save written before this change still loads and resolves as before.
- The `HexMapScene` held-hex detail panel and the between-sortie defence report show the left bot's stored armour/firepower/systems, the upgrade rating contribution and the total rating, alongside the existing hull and skill lines; `GymHexWar` leaves an upgraded bot through the same shared leave/derive/render code and displays the same numbers, with no divergent copy of the conversion (parity asserted by test).
- Tests cover: the mapping table (every id classified, unknown ids ignored), derivation totals, corrupt input (negative / fractional / non-finite snapshot collapses without throwing), the no-upgrades equality case, capture-cycle persistence and omission, `HexDefender` store round-trip/migration, and a `PlayScene`/`HexMapScene` assertion that a mini-boss victory persists the flown run's upgrades on the defender.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically GDD *capture cycle* step 3, the GDD defender-rating formula section, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (assumption A4) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` for the gym control surface.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who wins a hex can now leave behind a bot that keeps the permanent upgrades the ship had when the mini-boss fell, and can read on the map exactly what that bot is worth.

## Out of scope

- Changing `resolvePlayerStrength` or the `DEFAULT_FRONTIER_TUNING` constants (producer decision Q3 = A).
- Carrying the run's **temporary** (timed) weapons or field-pickup state into the defender.
- Carrying held minerals, score or remaining lives onto the defender (not upgrades — see Assumptions).
- Any new defender behaviour in combat: the bot is still never flown; the defence stays arithmetic over stored numbers.

## Verification (manual)

1. Deploy at an unheld hex from the map, deliberately collect several permanent upgrades during the sortie, then beat the wave-5 mini-boss.
2. Re-open the map, focus the newly held hex and confirm the detail panel lists the upgrade breakdown and a total rating greater than the bare-hull rating.
3. Run one between-sortie tick and confirm the defence report shows the same stored rating on the attack row.
4. Repeat in `GymHexWar`'s leave-bot control surface and confirm identical numbers.

## Constraints

- **Pure and injectable:** the conversion and the derivation stay in the pure core (`captureCycle` / `hangarEconomy`), no Phaser, no storage access; the scene only supplies the snapshot and persists the returned payload.
- **No schema version bump:** the new field is additive/optional and read by field presence, matching `skills`, `frontierTick` and the contract fields.
- **One rating formula:** the resolver keeps comparing one stored `defenceRating`; nothing new enters `resolveDefence`.
- **Producer decisions recorded in this intake:** Q1 = B (weapon levels + power-up levels + owned consumable charges), Q2 = B (hull weights: armour 3 / firepower 2 / systems 2 via a per-kind mapping table), Q3 = A (the frontier aggression budget is **unchanged** — defence simply gets easier).
- **Balance consequence accepted (Q3 = A):** with shipped tuning the attack strength tops out near 26–28, so an upgrade contribution in the tens makes a held hex mathematically unretakeable, and the between-sortie tick's retake pressure effectively disappears for well-defended hexes.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — new optional `HexDefender` upgrade-snapshot field (additive, omitted when empty).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — the mapping table, the snapshot → stat-bucket reducer and the extended rating derivation.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `HexCaptureInput` gains the snapshot; `leaveDefender` / `resolveHexCapture` thread it through and record it on the defender.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — supplies `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` / `snapshotConsumablePools()` at the mini-boss victory capture, in the same place the checkpoint snapshot is taken.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — defensive parsing of the new optional field (round-trip, migration by field presence).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` and `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` — intel lines and report numbers for the stored breakdown.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — renders the new intel lines (shared with the gym).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — the "leave bot" control surface passes the snapshot and shows the same numbers.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the rule change and its documented consequence.

## Related work

- Hangar War: capture cycle — hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6) — the module this changes.
- Pure defence resolver and frontier aggression clock (AH-0MVUXCA0J0011W88) — records the "rating from the hull's hangar upgrades, never a live battle" rule this item revises.
- Post-MVP Hangar War: upgraded defending bots with special skills (AH-0MVWZYJ740037EZ1) — the precedent for adding stored defender data additively.
- Versioned ai_hell_hangar_war store with migration (AH-0MVUXC0M5007LCGV) — the back-compat pattern the new optional field follows.
- Hangar economy and unlock tree (AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6) — owns `deriveDefenderRating`, the weights and `resolvePlayerStrength`.
- Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP) — the report surface that must show the new numbers.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance risk (highest):** with Q3 = A the frontier cannot outgrow upgraded defenders. A late run's upgrade contribution can exceed the maximum possible attack strength, so hexes become permanently safe and the war's retake tension goes quiet. *Mitigation:* the conversion lives in one exported table with one weight per bucket, so a follow-up tuning item can cap or rescale without touching saves; the risk should be measured from real runs before any such item is filed.
- **Save-compatibility risk:** an additive optional field on `HexDefender` must be omitted when empty and parsed defensively, or existing saves/fixtures drift. *Mitigation:* the `skills` pattern exactly; a store round-trip test and a "pre-change save loads unchanged" test.
- **Inflation risk:** consumable charge state changes between the mini-boss moment and the capture write if read at different points. *Mitigation:* read the whole snapshot once, in the same expression that feeds `resolveHexCapture`.
- **Design-document drift risk:** GDD step 3 and Candidate D A4 state the hangar-only rule; leaving them stale contradicts shipped behaviour. *Mitigation:* the docs AC names both files.
- **Scope-creep risk:** candidates deliberately excluded — changing `resolvePlayerStrength` (Q3 = A), retuning the frontier tuning constants, and carrying the run's *temporary* (timed) weapons into the defender. Each is a separate decision and must become its own work item rather than growing this one.
- **Assumption:** "permanent upgrades present at the end of the mini-boss battle" means the permanent levels and owned consumable charges the ship held at victory; held minerals, score and remaining lives are **not** upgrades and are not carried.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What counts as "all permanent upgrades"?** Options: (A) permanent weapon levels + power-up levels; (B) A plus owned consumable charge pools; (C) everything permanent including extra lives and held minerals. — **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **B** — permanent weapon levels, permanent power-up levels and owned consumable charges. *Research:* `playerPowerScore` (`src/core/difficultyScaling.ts`) already totals permanent weapon + power-up levels; `PowerUpLevelStore.snapshotConsumablePools()` exposes the owned consumable charge state.
- **Q2 — How do those upgrades become defence strength?** Options: (A) one documented weight per upgrade level; (B) reuse the hull weights (armour 3 / firepower 2 / systems 2) via a per-kind mapping; (C) apply them as boss-typed skills instead. — **Answer (operator):** **B** — keep one rating formula by mapping each weapon/power-up kind to armour, firepower or systems and applying the shipped weights. *Research:* `defenderRatingFromUpgrades(baseDefence, upgrades)` in `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` is the only rating formula; hull upgrades use armour/firepower/systems, so a per-kind mapping reuses it unchanged.
- **Q3 — Should the frontier aggression budget grow to match upgraded defenders?** Options: (A) leave the budget alone (defence gets easier); (B) count held defenders into `resolvePlayerStrength`; (C) cap the per-bot upgrade contribution. — **Answer (operator):** **A** — the budget is unchanged; the easier defence is accepted. *Research:* `resolvePlayerStrength` is fed from the hangar only, and tick attack strength derives from `baseAttackingForce: 2`, `forcePerOriginAggression: 1`, `aggressionPercentPerPoint: 15`, `jitterPercent: 10` (`DEFAULT_FRONTIER_TUNING`), i.e. a maximum near 26–28.
- **Q: How is "permanent" distinguished from a temporary field pickup at the victory moment?** — Answer (agent, from repo evidence): `Player.getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` report **permanent levels only** (`getTempWeaponIds()` / `getTempPowerUpIds()` are separate), so reading the permanent accessors at victory is exactly the requested set. No producer input needed.

data.description:
# Goal

As a player pushing into later rings, I want the **shipped** rings to actually
author hex variety (a personality, an optional contract and a ring landmark on
ordinary hexes), so the shipped machinery delivers the variety it was built for
instead of living only in the ring-3 verification sample.

Discovered from: AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG (post-MVP Hangar War: hex variety). The
epic shipped the vocabulary, loud validation, known-ahead intel, resolvers,
persistence and docs, and the authored example is the fixture sample
`VARIETY_RING_DEFINITIONS` in `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`.
The shipped table (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` + `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`
/ `hex-ring-2.csv`) still authors **no** variety, so no shipped hex currently
offers a player a personality, a contract or a landmark.

# Scope

- Author variety onto shipped hexes as a **data change only**: extend
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` and mirror it in the CSV seeds (the parity
  test guards drift). No new code path — the vocabulary and validation already
  ship.
- Suggested minimum shape (producer to confirm): one personality on a ring-2
  hex, one optional contract on a ring-2 hex, and one landmark (`fortress` or
  `cache`) on a ring-2 hex. Ring 1 stays the tutorial ring and keeps its plain
  six chores unless the producer says otherwise.
- Landmark/contract rewards must stay inside the ring-2 survivable aggression
  band (AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC) and inside the existing economy (salvage/cores
  through `bankSalvage`; no new currency), and must respect the one-weapon-hex
  rule (a `cache` can never be the weapon hex — already validated).
- Update GDD §8.2 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` to show which shipped
  hexes author variety.

# Acceptance Criteria

- At least one personality, one optional contract and one landmark are authored
  on shipped ring-2 hexes in `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` and mirrored in
  the CSV seeds (parity test green).
- `validateRingDefinitions(1|2, HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS)` stays green, and the
  shipped-data tests assert the authored variety is published by
  `buildHexMapModel` before commitment.
- Ring 2's measured timings stay inside its survivable band (the ring-timing
  evaluation is re-measured and recorded).
- Docs (GDD §8.2, `OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`) name the shipped variety hexes.
- Full suite green on dev.

# Key Files

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`, `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` (validation only — no code change expected)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` (no change expected — read model already
  publishes the axes)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8.2), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` + `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` (re-measure)

# Impact

Players will finally meet the variety the Hangar War was built for: a ring-2
hex that fights differently, one that offers an optional contract for extra
banked salvage, and one set-piece capture that needs two passes or pays out
instead of granting.

# Related work

- discovered-from: AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG (hex variety epic — machinery shipped)
- AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC — ring 2 survivable aggression band
- AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55 — special missions (special rewards stay there)
